quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit if the road is wet, slippery, or if you cannot see well. Anything that makes conditions worse means you should slow down. You can get a ticket for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are within the speed limit.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on the left and a bicycle is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you have two hazards, deal with one at a time. Do not try to squeeze between both the car and the bike. Wait for the car to pass first, then pass the bicycle.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for an hour or more.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery at the start of rain because water brings oil up from the asphalt. This problem gets worse in hot weather, when heat and water bring more oil to the surface.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn of railroad crossings. This sign tells you a railroad crossing is coming. Watch for trains.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross these lines to pass another vehicle if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a curve or hill because traffic is unlikely to come.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
If there is a solid yellow line next to you and the other lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on a curve or hill because you cannot see oncoming traffic and may crash. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not pass across a solid yellow line.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow to a stop.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not hit the brakes right away. Grip the wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down by releasing the gas. Once you are going slowly, brake gently and pull to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what other cars do, not the flagger.
Assume the flagger should not be there.

questions.explanation: Always follow flaggers, signs, and police in construction zones. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right side and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
Give them the right-of-way only when they have the legal right.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop severe bleeding. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: After an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop at or near the accident scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because other vehicles could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Signal when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your hazard lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, let traffic and pedestrians pass, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: All people in a moving vehicle must wear a seat belt. Children under six years old or weighing less than 60 pounds must use an approved child safety seat.

questions.question: To enter a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal before merging. Match the speed of traffic and always yield to other vehicles.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane.
questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle, even if there appears to be room. Motorcyclists need the full lane width to move safely.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:

options.text: Pass the animal as closely as possible.

questions.explanation: Be very careful around animals on the road. Pass slowly to avoid scaring the animal.

questions.question: What is a "No zone?"

options.text: The blind spot of a large vehicle
An area designated for motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle
questions.explanation: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Avoid staying in these blind spots.

questions.question: A curb painted ____ means you can park there for only a limited time.
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking rules. A green curb means you can park for a limited time. A nearby sign shows how long you can park.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: What should you do when another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This encourages the tailgater to pass you.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, move to the right if possible. If not, slow down gradually when it is safe. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: A construction area is coming up.

questions.explanation: A solid edge line marks where the road ends. If this line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has a series of turns and curves.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. You should yield and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lane and need to pass a cyclist going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving plenty of space between your vehicle and the cyclist.
Continue straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to warn the cyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving plenty of space between your vehicle and the cyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space from your mirror to the cyclist, or 5 feet on higher speed roads or when passing a group. Honking can startle cyclists and cause them to crash.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to use:

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: On a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you use to turn left?
questions.explanation: To turn left on multilane streets and highways, start from the left lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well in advance. Start slowing down only after you enter the exit lane, not before.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light require you to do?
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at any stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
Try to get to the front of any slow-moving traffic so that you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers to your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the risk of a collision. If you drive faster than surrounding traffic, you will have to pass repeatedly. Drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit, and pass only when needed.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering the roadway.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with the traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: What maneuvers can you perform from the center lane?
questions.explanation: The center lane is reserved for left-turning vehicles only. You cannot use it for passing or for driving straight through.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the light like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights appear at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: What should you do before starting your car's engine?

options.text: Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure all of the vehicle's occupants have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure all of the vehicle's occupants have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting your engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also coming to the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic go, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells you a traffic light is coming, so be ready for red or yellow lights.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: When you drive fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and slide on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
questions.explanation: Road conditions affect how well you can stop. Slow down when roads are slippery or wet so you can control your car and stop safely.

questions.question: The light is green and you want to turn left, but traffic coming toward you is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the edge of the intersection for traffic to pass.
Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to pass.
Go because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to pass.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for that traffic to pass first. You can move into the intersection when the light is green, but do not turn until it is safe.

questions.question: When driving past parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for people or cars to suddenly come into your lane.
Expect all drivers and people to see you and give you space.
Honk your horn to warn drivers and people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for people or cars to suddenly come into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance from parked cars. A person may step out suddenly, or a driver may pull out without seeing you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and use your horn.
You are entering a school parking lot.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a school zone is ahead. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: Failure to yield the right-of-way is the leading cause of accidents in Nevada.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way laws help traffic move safely through intersections. Failing to yield the right-of-way causes the most accidents in Nevada.

questions.question: If you are moving with other vehicles across railroad tracks, it is safe to stop on the tracks for a short time.
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross railroad tracks if your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time. Which one must yield?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on the right.
